'''Pecheneg''' is an extinct [[Turkic languages|Turkic language]] spoken by the [[Pechenegs]] in [[Eastern Europe]] (parts of [[Southern Ukraine]], [[Southern Russia]], [[Moldova]], [[Romania]] and [[Hungary]]) in the 7th–12th centuries. However, names in this language (Beke, Wochun, Lechk, etc.) are reported from [[Hatvan]] until 1290.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wenzel |first=Gusztáv |url=https://archive.org/details/codexdiplomatic20wenzgoog/page/n165/mode/1up |title=Codex diplomaticus Arpadianus continuatus =: Árpádkori új okmánytár |publisher=Eggenberger Ferdinánd Akademiai |year=1860 |location=Harvard University |pages=108 |language=Latin}}</ref> 

== Classification ==
Due to poor documentation and the absence of any descendant languages,  linguists have been prevented from making an accurate classification. It is placed as unclassified in the [[Kipchak languages|Kipchak]] language family in [[Glottolog]] and in the Kipchak–Cuman language family in [[Linguist List]].

[[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] princess [[Anna Komnene]] asserts that the Pechenegs and [[Cumans]] spoke the same language,<ref>{{cite book|last1=Howorth|first1=Henry Hoyle|title=History of the Mongols|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gJsUAQAAIAAJ&q=pecheneg+language&pg=PA4|year=1880|publisher=Burt Franklin |isbn=9780343146429 |access-date=15 May 2016}}</ref> while Mahmud al-Kashgari considered their language to be a corrupted form of Turkic. Most contemporary researchers conclude that they spoke a [[Common Turkic languages|Common Turkic language]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Paroń |first=Aleksander |title=The Pechenegs : nomads in the political and cultural landscape of Medieval Europe |date=2021 |others=Thomas Anessi |isbn=978-90-04-44109-5 |location=Leiden |oclc=1245959323}}</ref>
